jobs_results.description:
About Mach Industries




Founded in 2023, Mach Industries is a rapidly growing defense technology company focused on developing next-generation autonomous defense platforms. At the core of our mission is the commitment to delivering scalable, decentralized defense systems that enhance the strategic capabilities of the United States and its allies. With a workforce of approximately 350 employees, we operate with startup agility and ambition.




Our vision is to redefine the future of warfare through cutting-edge manufacturing, innovation at speed, and unwavering focus on national security. We are dedicated to solving the next generation of warfare with lethal systems that deter kinetic conflict and protect global security.



The Role




We are seeking a engineer to join our new and non-defense consumer robotics program. Robotic hands are a dedicated area of development for our group and this role offers significant ownership in solving challenges related to handling everyday objects with different shapes, weights, and textures. Our robotics engineers work end to end to build complete systems, partnering closely with mechanical, electrical, and software engineers to turn concepts into products. 

Key Responsibilities



 Make early architecture and component decisions with safety, manufacturability, reliability, and serviceability in mind
 Own decisions about mechanisms that determine dexterity, strength, and range of motion
 Develop and tune hand controls so the robot can grasp securely, adjust its grip, and handle fragile or unfamiliar objects
 Champion systems integration by partnering with electrical, mechanical, and software peers to bring the complete hand system to life
 Conduct rigorous reliability testing, failure analysis, and root-cause investigations, using experiments and analysis to guide the next design
Required Qualifications 



 Experience designing robotic hand mechanisms and actuator control systems
 Demonstrated hands-on experience turning ideas into hardware and bridging theory and practice
 Experience taking ambiguous, open-ended problems and creating workable designs
 Intrinsic curiosity about hard problems and the motivation to learn unfamiliar systems
 Ability to lead reviews, influence cross-functional teams, and communicate risks and solutions clearly
 Bachelor's degree in electrical engineering, mechatronics, mechanical engineering, computer science, robotics, physics, or a related engineering discipline
Preferred Qualifications 



 Advanced understanding of robotic hand mechanisms, kinematics, dynamics, and motion and force control.
 Experience with compact motor-transmission assemblies, tendon-driven or linkage-based fingers, force or tactile sensing, and grasp stability
 Familiarity with robotic hardware such as actuators, gearboxes, motors, bearings and sensors
 Hands-on prototyping skills and experience troubleshooting mechanical and electromechanical systems
 Knowledge of reliability testing, failure analysis, and root-cause investigations
 Hands-on experience using structural FEA to drive design optimization, including stiffness, strength, and mass optimization
 Strong understanding of mechanical design principles, materials, manufacturing processes, GD&T, and tolerance analysis
 Proficiency with 3D CAD software such as Onshape, SolidWorks, Creo, NX, CATIA, or similar tools.
 3+ years of experience taking robotic or electromechanical hardware from concept through validation and deployment.
Additional Requirements





 Available to work extended hours and weekends as needed





To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. job_highlights.title: Responsibilities
items: We need an exceptional robotics engineer to make robots assemble harnesses reliably
You’ll focus on robot and end-effector programming, machine vision and manipulation
The work is physical and unforgiving: finding a small contact, handling a flexible wire, aligning it with a connector and inserting it correctly
Then knowing whether it worked, recovering when it didn’t and doing it thousands of times

jobs_results.description:
At Loombotic, we’re automating wire harness manufacturing.


We need an exceptional robotics engineer to make robots assemble harnesses reliably. You’ll focus on robot and end-effector programming, machine vision and manipulation.


The work is physical and unforgiving: finding a small contact, handling a flexible wire, aligning it with a connector and inserting it correctly. Then knowing whether it worked, recovering when it didn’t and doing it thousands of times.


You’ll own the software that connects perception to action: camera calibration, visual localization, motion, end-effector control and verification. You’ll work closely with our mechatronics team to improve the hardware and software together.


We have 20,000 square feet of factory to automate, with a goal of producing hundreds of thousands of harnesses per month by mid-2027.


You should be comfortable moving between code, cameras and real hardware, and staying with a problem until the machine works consistently.


We use AI agents wherever they make engineering better.

jobs_results.description:
Arm is building a Robotics Research Lab in Austin to explore the technologies required to enable the next generation of intelligent, general-purpose robots!

 

We are looking for a Staff Robotics Research Engineer with a strong research background in one or more areas of robotics and an interest in working across traditional disciplinary boundaries. Relevant areas include robot learning and embodied AI, perception and sensor fusion, planning and decision making, control and optimization, safety and formal methods, robot systems, and mechatronics!

 

Our research is motivated by a fundamental question: what does it take to build robots that can act competently in the real world? Answering this requires advances within individual robotics capabilities, but also new ways of combining them into coherent intelligent systems. We are particularly interested in researchers who want to explore the interfaces between disciplines: learning and planning, perception and action, reasoning and control, safety and autonomy, software and hardware.

 

This is a hands-on research role. You will develop new methods, implement them on real robotic platforms, and work with researchers across disciplines to build and evaluate complete robotic systems. The results will both advance the state of the art in robotics and help shape future Arm technologies for Physical AI.

jobs_results.description:
Alliance Automation began operations in August 2008, seizing an opportunity to provide automation solutions to underserved industries. Our innovative thinkers design and build robotic automation systems that optimize production processes. We provide automation solutions for a multitude of industries; each helping upgrade efficiency, increase throughput and guarantee reliability in production.

Job Description:

POSITION OVERVIEW

Alliance Automation is seeking a Robotics Engineer to design, program, commission, and 

support industrial robotic systems used in custom automation equipment.

This position is intended for an automation professional with strong hands-on robotic

programming, integration, troubleshooting, and commissioning experience. The Robotics 

Engineer will take technical ownership of robotic applications while working closely with Controls 

Engineers, Mechanical and Electrical Designers, Machine Assembly, Applications, Project 

Management, and customers.

The Robotics Engineer supports projects from concept and simulation through programming, 

integration, runoff, installation, and customer acceptance. This position is expected to remain 

hands-on and capable of solving difficult robotic application and integration problems both at 

Alliance Automation and at customer facilities.

TOP 5 RESPONSIBILITIES

Robot Programming and Commissioning

Program, configure, commission, and troubleshoot industrial robotic systems for material handling, machine tending, assembly, dispensing, welding, palletizing, vision-guided applications, and other automated processes.

Robotic System Integration

Integrate robots with PLC/PAC systems, machine controls, safety systems, vision systems, end-of-arm tooling, servo equipment, industrial networks, and other automation components.

Application Development and Optimization

Develop robot programs, motion strategies, frames, payload configurations, recovery routines, and application-specific logic. Optimize robot motion, cycle time, reliability, and overall system performance.

Technical Project Execution

Support robotic applications from concept through customer acceptance. Identify technical risks, assist with project planning, support machine integration, and help projects meet performance, schedule, and customer requirements.

Standards, Support, and Knowledge Sharing

Develop and improve robotic programming standards, reusable routines, documentation, troubleshooting practices, and commissioning methods. Share robotic knowledge with Controls Engineers and technicians to increase the overall robotics capability of Alliance Automation.

ADDITIONAL RESPONSIBILITIES / DUTIES

Program and commission industrial robots and associated automation equipment.

Develop robot programs, frames, tool data, payloads, motion paths, I/O interfaces, and recovery routines.

Configure and integrate robot controllers with PLC/PAC systems and industrial networks.

Integrate robot safety functions with machine safety systems and applicable safety devices.

Configure and support robot-based and external machine-vision applications.

Support end-of-arm tooling development, integration, setup, and troubleshooting.

Optimize robot paths, motion parameters, cycle time, and application performance.

Develop safe and effective automatic recovery and fault-handling strategies.

Conduct robotic application reviews and identify potential technical risks before build and commissioning.

Support robot simulation, reach studies, cycle-time analysis, and application feasibility when required.

Assist Controls Engineers with robotic integration and troubleshooting.

Lead troubleshooting and root-cause analysis of difficult robotic and automation issues.

Support Applications with robotic concepts, technology selection, feasibility reviews, quotations, and labor estimates.

Participate in machine runoff, installation, commissioning, training, and customer acceptance.

Develop and maintain robotic programming standards, templates, documentation, and reusable solutions.

Provide technical guidance and knowledge sharing to engineers and technicians.

Travel to customer facilities for installation, commissioning, troubleshooting, training, and production support.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS/EXPERIENCE

Five or more years of industrial robotics, controls, or automation experience preferred.

Related engineering or technical degree, or equivalent technical education and work experience.

Advanced programming and troubleshooting capability with at least one major industrial robot platform.

Experience with FANUC, Yaskawa, ABB, Kawasaki, KUKA, or similar industrial robotic systems.

Strong understanding of robotic motion, coordinate systems, frames, payloads, tooling, I/O, and application programming.

Experience integrating robots with PLC/PAC systems and industrial networks.

Working knowledge of machine safety and robotic safety systems.

Experience with machine vision, vision-guided robotics, or robotic inspection applications preferred.

Experience with servo systems, end-of-arm tooling, and other automation equipment preferred.

Ability to diagnose complex robotic, electrical, controls, and process-related problems.

Ability to estimate robotic programming, commissioning, and site-support labor requirements.

Strong analytical, troubleshooting, and root-cause problem-solving skills.

Ability to communicate technical information clearly to engineers, customers, leadership, and other departments.

Willingness to remain hands-on with programming, commissioning, troubleshooting, and field support.

Ability to adapt to shifting priorities and travel to customer facilities as required.

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

A successful Robotics Engineer does more than program robots.

This person takes ownership of robotic applications, develops reliable and maintainable solutions, reduces commissioning time, improves cycle time and equipment performance, identifies technical risks before they become project problems, and helps increase the robotics capability of the entire Controls Engineering team.

The result is robotic systems that are safe, reliable, maintainable, efficient, and ready to perform in production.

WHAT WE OFFER

 Alliance Automation benefits include, but are not limited to:

Paid Vacation

Sick Time

Medical/Dental/Vision/Life/Disability

401k & Company Match

Parental Leave
